proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access target override / paired bearer targeting
proposed_widenings.justification: The item does not grant a normal unrestricted cast of Sending. It changes the spell's legal target to the bearer of the paired stone.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The target is the bearer of the other stone.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access availability gate on paired bearer presence
proposed_widenings.justification: The cast is conditionally blocked when no creature bears the paired stone. The current surface can say an item grants spell access, but not that the cast fizzles before happening under a closed precondition.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If no creature bears the other stone, you know that fact as soon as you use the stone, and you don't cast the spell.

proposed_widenings.name: paired-item invalidation lifecycle
proposed_widenings.justification: The item's remaining magic depends on the continued existence of its paired counterpart. Current destruction modeling only covers self-exhaustion / last-charge destruction, not cross-item dependency.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If one of the stones in a pair is destroyed, the other one becomes nonmagical.

notes: Magic item + activation family is the right broad fit, but authoring an unrestricted Sending cast would be false. I did not create content files because the current surface cannot express the paired-target constraint, the no-bearer no-cast gate, or the cross-stone invalidation rule honestly.
